issues.description: The problem specification requires a public method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (used by orderMeal to attempt serving queued orders). The provided solution implements this behavior in a method named processOrders() and does not provide checkOrderReady(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students (and may cause tests that expect checkOrderReady() to fail) because the expected method is missing or differently named.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution and template match the specification: rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (keeping its behavior and visibility) and ensure orderMeal calls checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, update the problem statement and tests to reference processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady() so names are consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named checkOrderReady() (UML and text) that orderMeal() should call to try serving queued orders. The reference solution implements this behavior in a method named processOrders() and orderMeal() calls processOrders() instead. This naming divergence (checkOrderReady vs processOrders) refers to the same conceptual operation but uses different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students mapping the requirements to the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same method name as specified in the problem statement. Rename processOrders() to checkOrderReady() in the solution (and update its callers), or add a public checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(), so the identifier matches the problem description.
